stories.headline: NMC endorses lifestyle changes over GLP-1 drugs in child obesity fight
stories.text: The Nordic Medicines Council on Wednesday issued its first global guidelines on obesity in children. It recommended diet, exercise and counselling ahead of weight-loss drugs. GLP-1 drugs may be considered for adolescents aged 10 to 19 only after supervised programmes have failed; for children under 10 it advised against medication because of doubts over long-term safety. Council figures show 2.4 million people aged 5 to 19 in the region lived with obesity in 2025. Halden Pharma's Slimra is approved for some adolescents aged 12 and older in the United States and the European Union.

stories.headline: UPDATE 2-DOJ probes Corvex's licensing deal with AI startup Vantir, Valley Ledger reports
stories.text: The US Justice Department has opened an inquiry into Corvex's agreement to license technology from AI chip start-up Vantir and hire some of its staff, the Valley Ledger reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Corvex agreed the deal in December. Corvex declined to comment.

stories.headline: UPDATE 1-Corvex plans major expansion of data centre capacity in Canada
stories.text: Corvex plans to expand data centre capacity in Canada with local partners, the company said, without giving a cost.
